clue.text: Most unusual — Don shot within old part of Wales

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the other piece
most of a word, not all of it, so its final letter is dropped
something shot is wrecked or ruined, so those letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A university don has been shot dead in a strange incident somewhere in rural Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: RARE loses its last letter to RAR, which holds the scrambled DON. Radnorshire was a Welsh county, abolished in 1974 and now part of Powys.
explanation.definitionFit: Radnor (Radnorshire) was a historic county in mid-Wales, no longer an administrative unit.

clue.text: Organised crime largely has a compelling attraction

indicators.note: organised means put into a new arrangement, so the letters that follow are rearranged
largely means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, shortened by one letter

explanation.surface: Organised crime holds a dangerous glamour that draws people in.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIME loses its E, then CRIM plus HAS A are rearranged. 'has a' looks like a link but its letters are all needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is the personal magnetism or charm that makes someone powerfully appealing to others.

clue.text: Old German choirs essentially welcoming sopranos

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece goes inside the other
essentially points to the essence or heart of the word, its central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of choirs
S is the abbreviation for soprano, twice for the plural

explanation.surface: Choirs in old Germany took on extra sopranos.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossi is German slang for an East German; after reunification the old GDR citizens make it 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossi is the colloquial German term for someone from the former East Germany, a vanished state.

clue.text: Door may suffer damage in hospital's communal area

indicators.note: a door that suffers damage is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a hospital door might get bashed in a busy shared space.
explanation.definitionFit: A day room is a lounge in a hospital or institution where patients sit together during the day.

clue.text: Bird talking nonsense more than once

indicators.note: talking means we judge the word by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense, said twice

explanation.surface: A parrot or mynah babbling nonsense over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird talking' suggests a parrot, but the bird is the definition and talking signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulbul is a songbird of Africa and Asia, famed in Persian poetry as the nightingale.

clue.text: Promotion project has worker assisting officer

parts.note: to project is to stick out
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A promotion scheme gives a staff member the job of helping a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' and 'officer' suggest a military rank; promotion is advertising here.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is a military officer who acts as administrative aide to a commanding officer.

clue.text: Cry of dismay — American has grand stolen in Danish city

indicators.note: something stolen is taken away, so that letter goes missing

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: An American wails after a thousand pounds is stolen from them in Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars, shortened to G. 'has' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aarhus is Denmark's second-largest city, on the east coast of Jutland.

clue.text: Shocks regarding money female spent

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at how a woman has spent the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' looks like the woman's action with the money, but it tells you to drop the letter for female.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone is to amaze or stun them, so it is a verb synonym of shocks.

clue.text: I'm after sick note for a limited period

indicators.note: sick means unwell and out of sorts, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone after a sick note to get off work for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm after sick note' reads as wanting a doctor's note; 'sick' is the anagram signal and the note is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A time frame is a fixed span of time within which something must happen.

clue.text: Getting more twisted, called for revolution — it's not true resistance

definitions.note: the answer is a comparative adjective; 'getting' only frames it

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An escalating political row over who called for revolution and who resisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called for revolution' reads as a demand for uprising; 'for' is just a link and revolution turns the word for called round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarly means knotted and twisted like old wood, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Crime gang is protecting a little ugly guy who worked on Strip

parts.note: a mob is a criminal gang

indicators.note: protecting means shielding, wrapping round what it guards
a little of the word means just its first letter

explanation.surface: A mafia gang shields an unattractive man who once worked on the Las Vegas Strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Strip sound like the Las Vegas Strip; it is the one-sided Möbius strip.
explanation.definitionFit: August Möbius, German mathematician, described the one-sided surface now called the Möbius strip.

clue.text: Love reciprocated — very touching

indicators.note: reciprocated means returned, given back the other way

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A love returned in kind, which is very moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very touching' reads as moving; touching here means concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, and the word also names erotic or sexual desire.

clue.text: Film followed different women being evicted — talk at length about it

indicators.note: about it means surrounding the rest of the wordplay
evicted means thrown out, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: to gas is to chatter on and on

indicators.note: different means changed, so those letters take another order

explanation.surface: A film plot in which various women are thrown out of their homes, which everyone then chatters about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed' looks like the film's plot verb, but it is the anagram fodder; 'it' in the last part means everything before.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodfellas is Martin Scorsese's 1990 gangster movie about the New York mob.

clue.text: Dead loud — one made man beginning to rant about boss

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is used
about means going round the other pieces

parts.note: got means made, as in got ready
F is forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: A mafia boss rants about a very loud informer who became a made man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made man' looks like a Mafia term, but the two words split. A made man is a fully initiated Mafia member, and the boss is who made him.
explanation.definitionFit: A godfather is the head of a Mafia family, its chief or leader.

clue.text: Touching game a naughty kid played outside

indicators.note: outside means wrapped round the other piece
played means fooled about with, so these letters change places

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child playing a game outdoors that involves touching others.
explanation.walkthrough: KID becomes KDI and goes round A BAD. Kabaddi is a South Asian team sport where raiders tag opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabaddi is a contact team sport from South Asia in which a raider scores by tagging opponents.

clue.text: Trouble, yet kept working in plant

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: yet and but both mean however

explanation.surface: Despite difficulties, someone carried on working at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutilon is a genus of flowering shrubs in the mallow family, often called flowering maple.

clue.text: Old creature hurt not a single flier

indicators.note: not a single means without one, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: a moth is a flying insect

explanation.surface: An aged animal injured, yet not one bird or insect flying.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIM without I (one), then MOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The mammoth is an extinct elephant-like animal of the Ice Age, hence an ancient beast.

clue.text: Do more at work though not too quickly

indicators.note: work as a verb means to knead or fashion, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to work harder, but without rushing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderato is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate pace, neither fast nor slow.

clue.text: Shooter provided round back — money on completion

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word is read backwards
on completion means at the very end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A hitman's terms: paid in full once the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money on completion' reads as payment terms; it gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooter is slang for a gun, and a firearm is any portable gun.

clue.text: Make habitual errors initially as tout — I'm a fool

indicators.note: to fool about is to mess around, so the letters are scrambled
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: A ticket tout confesses to being an idiot who keeps making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout is a ticket scalper. 'fool' looks like a noun in 'I'm a fool', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To automatise an action is to make it automatic, done by habit without conscious thought.

clue.text: It should discourage singers — what might they be doing outside?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: something that puts off choristers

definitions.text: what might they be doing outside?
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: singers are informers to the police, and the mob's code of silence makes them pay for talking

explanation.surface: Something that deters people from carolling in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is underworld slang for informing; the Mafia's code of silence forbids it, and the clue's question hints at the grim fate of anyone who breaks it.
explanation.definitionFit: Omertà is the Mafia's code of silence, forbidding members from giving information to the authorities.

clue.text: One's bad words about Parliament

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: mud is slander, as in mudslinging

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about the foul language heard in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duma is the lower house of Russia's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duma is the elected legislative assembly of Russia, in tsarist times and today.

clue.text: Frenzied woman's grabbed another

indicators.note: grabbed means seized and held, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: another woman, taken from the definition: Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A crazed woman has seized hold of someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The words do double duty: 'Frenzied' gives MAD and 'another' means another woman, Ena, harking back to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the wild female followers of Dionysus, and the word now means any frenzied woman.

clue.text: Sophisticated bash at City hotel

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A smart party held at a hotel in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a party, but it means a blow. The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech describes advanced, technologically sophisticated equipment or design.

clue.text: English fellow in tight corner (he will get things done)

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
tight is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Englishman in a tight spot, with a note that he gets the job done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight corner' reads as a fix, but tight signals the anagram of corner, with F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An enforcer is a heavy hired to make people comply, often with violence, as in gangland.

clue.text: Camorra effectively giving rise to this

definitions.text: Camorra effectively giving rise to this

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the letters read upwards, bottom to top
effectively here means in effect contained, the letters lie across the words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: The Neapolitan mafia's real power lies in the dread it creates.
explanation.walkthrough: The Camorra is the Naples crime syndicate. The whole clue is the definition: what it produces is terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimidation is how a criminal syndicate rules, so dread is exactly what it produces.

clue.text: 24 may be wrong — they both suggest hesitation

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: An enforcer could be mistaken, judging by their hesitancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is ENFORCER. 'they both' refers to two hesitation noises, UR and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob heavy may inflict pain to extract information, making him one who tortures.

clue.text: Train people to drive tram … and boat? That's not right

indicators.note: to drive is to push about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: not right means without R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Railway staff being taught to drive trams and boats, which seems wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAM is rearranged, then ARK loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Amtrak is the US national passenger rail operator, so its staff are train people.
